Customer (James Baker): I haven't had a bill from you in months, and now my service has been cut off.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Hi James Baker, Nomsa Khumalo here — let me pull that up.
Customer (James Baker): Can I actually pay this all at once, or is there a plan to spread it out?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): I'm sorry, that's a lot to deal with. Let me go through the history properly.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (James Baker): Sure, it's the house on the account, and the bill's in my name.
Customer (James Baker): How does a bill just not get sent for that long without anyone catching it?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): When did you move into the property?
Customer (James Baker): Last winter. We're renting.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Who were you paying utilities to?
Customer (James Baker): The city. I assumed gas was included.

Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): To recap: the balance is on a twelve-month plan, the set-up error is recorded against us, and regular bills start next cycle.
Customer (James Baker): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Kevin Ross): So one of them was actually wrong?
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Yes, a late-payment charge was applied after your payment had already cleared. That's the adjustment.
Customer (Kevin Ross): And the zero-usage charges?
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Those are regulated and stay. The breakdown in your email explains each one.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): To recap: the late-payment charge comes off on your next statement, and the line-by-line breakdown is in your email.
Customer (Kevin Ross): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
